disease_label_per_paper: Acute rheumatic fever with atypical arthritis, subcutaneous nodules, and carditis
presentation_summary: 13-year-old boy presented after 3 years of intermittent fever with recurrent upper-respiratory infections and prolonged joint pain, with marked exacerbation for 2 months before admission.

Articular symptoms were atypical for classic ARF: initially ankles, then knees and cervical/lumbosacral spine, later shoulders, elbows, MCP/PIP joints, wrists, knees, and ankles; pain was bilateral symmetric, nonmigratory, worse at rest and terminal movement, with difficulty sitting, turning in bed, moving the neck, and flexing limbs.
He noticed hard swellings for 10 days over the forehead, occiput, and extensor forearms; exam showed multiple painless 0.5-2 cm nodules.

Admission temperature was 101 F, respiratory rate 24/min, heart rate 94/min, and blood pressure 113/60 mmHg. Joint tenderness was widespread, but the paper states there was no swelling, redness, deformity, rash, dyspnea, chest pain, hemoptysis, choreiform movement, eye redness, urinary symptoms, travel to hilly areas, or bloody diarrhea.

Cardiac exam showed an apical pansystolic murmur radiating to the axilla and a diastolic murmur over the left parasternal area. CBC and inflammatory markers were obtained on admission. ASO/anti-DNase B, Doppler echocardiography, histopathology of nodules, and final Jones adjudication are preserved as confirmatory/non-ranking context.

risk_context.source_text_value: case reported from India, an ARF-endemic setting
history of recurrent episodes of upper respiratory tract infections with fever for the same duration

observations.source_text_value: fever intermittent, rising to 103 F, usually lasting for a week
generalized musculoskeletal pain with difficulty turning in bed and flexing the limbs
tenderness in lower thoracic and lumbar spine, bilateral wrist, PIP, MCP, elbow, knee, and ankle
bilaterally symmetrical, nonmigratory, prolonged arthritis with small-joint and axial involvement and poor salicylate response
there was no swelling, redness or deformity at any joint
multiple swelling on the ulnar side of the forearm, frontal bone and occiput of the skull that were nontender
pansystolic murmur grade 2-3/6 on the apex radiating to the axilla and diastolic murmur grade 3/6 over the left parasternal area
cardiac murmurs compatible with mitral and aortic valvular involvement on presentation

confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: thickened mitral valve with moderate mitral regurgitation
echogenic aortic valve with mild regurgitation

confirmatory_findings.finding: Paper diagnosis by revised Jones criteria
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: A diagnosis of ARF was made on the basis of revised Jones criteria
Throat swab and blood cultures were sterile while HLA-B27, ANA, rheumatoid factor were negative

outcome.clinical_course: Pain relief required 6 weeks of therapy; nodules enlarged initially for 2 weeks then disappeared by about 8 weeks. At 6 months on penicillin prophylaxis, the patient was asymptomatic with no residual joint deformities.
outcome.source_text_value: complete pain relief being obtained by 6 weeks ... nodules ... disappear by almost 8 weeks ... on penicillin prophylaxis for the past 6 months and is asymptomatic

quality_warnings: ASO, anti-DNase B, Doppler echo findings, histopathology, and final Jones adjudication are retained as confirmatory_findings with use_in_ranking:false.
Atypical arthritis pattern is preserved rather than rewritten as classic migratory arthritis.
